<!-- Literature cards for lecture 21: one neuron and small fully connected
     networks in published geoscience. Edit THIS file to update the papers;
     the deck includes it verbatim. Each card: the layer sizes first
     (inputs-hidden-outputs), one sentence, then the citation. Crossref records
     checked 2026-11-15, except Dowla et al. (no Crossref record; OSTI 7283112).
     Numbers read from: Dowla, abstract; Picchiani, Sauzede, Ntokas, full text;
     Pearson, arXiv 1706.04319; aftershocks, our rerun (figscripts/aftershock_auc_rerun.py). -->

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.lit-card}
[1 neuron]{.lit-num}

[Solid Earth. Where aftershocks occur: a network of 13,451 weights and a single neuron fed one stress quantity reach the same score (AUC 0.849 and 0.847 in our rerun).]{.lit-msg}

[DeVries, P. M. R., et al. (2018). *Nature*, 560, 632–634. Mignan, A., & Broccardo, M. (2019). One neuron versus deep learning in aftershock prediction. *Nature*, 574, E1–E3.]{.lit-cite}
:::

::: {.lit-card}
[82-1-2]{.lit-num}

[Solid Earth. Earthquake or nuclear test, from 82 spectral values at one station: one hidden neuron classifies over 93% of unseen events correctly, similar to a linear discriminant.]{.lit-msg}

[Dowla, F. U., Taylor, S. R., & Anderson, R. W. (1990). Seismic discrimination with artificial neural networks. *Bull. Seismol. Soc. Am.*, 80(5), 1346–1373.]{.lit-cite}
:::

::: {.lit-card}
[3-10-2]{.lit-num}

[Volcanoes. Ash or no ash in satellite images of Etna eruptions, from three thermal infrared channels: detection accuracy above 90% against the method that labeled the training pixels.]{.lit-msg}

[Picchiani, M., et al. (2011). Volcanic ash detection and retrievals using MODIS data by means of neural networks. *Atmos. Meas. Tech.*, 4, 2619–2631. CC BY 3.0.]{.lit-cite}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.lit-card}
[9-20-17-1]{.lit-num}

[Ocean. Nitrate from temperature, salinity, pressure, oxygen, position and date, trained on 549,561 bottle samples: error 1.04 µmol/kg. Profiling floats can then report nutrients they do not measure.]{.lit-msg}

[Sauzède, R., et al. (2017). Estimates of water-column nutrient concentrations and carbonate system parameters in the global ocean. *Front. Mar. Sci.*, 4, 128. CC BY.]{.lit-cite}
:::

::: {.lit-card}
[12-120-1]{.lit-num}

[Land water. Snow water equivalent from snow depth at 2,878 Canadian locations: mean absolute error 32.8, against 44.5 for the better of two regression formulas.]{.lit-msg}

[Ntokas, K. F. F., et al. (2021). Investigating ANN architectures and training to estimate snow water equivalent from snow depth. *Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci.*, 25, 3017–3040. CC BY 4.0.]{.lit-cite}
:::

::: {.lit-card}
[180-64-32-8-1]{.lit-num}

[Exoplanets. Transit or no transit in a light curve of 180 points: the fully connected network finds 88.7% of simulated transits, a convolutional network 88.5%, the box-fitting search 63.1%.]{.lit-msg}

[Pearson, K. A., Palafox, L., & Griffith, C. A. (2018). Searching for exoplanets using artificial intelligence. *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.*, 474, 478–491.]{.lit-cite}
:::
:::
